title: Reactivity series and displacement; Halide ions; Empirical and molecular formulae
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RX09#t1 term and clue written for the game; RX09#t2 term and clue written for the game; PT06#t4 term and clue written for the game; PT06#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM02#N.3, PT06#N.3, RX09#N.2, AM02#N.5, PT06#N.5, RX09#N.6, AM02#N.7a, PT06#N.10, RX09#N.8, AM02#N.11, PT06#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Oxidising agent
items.clue: Role of halogens, which react by gaining electrons: X₂ + 2e⁻ → 2X⁻.

items.label: Reducing agent
items.clue: Role of metals, which react by losing electrons, as Zn does with Cu²⁺.

items.label: Precipitate
items.clue: Insoluble product, such as AgX(s), that appears when Ag⁺(aq) meets X⁻(aq).

items.label: Silver nitrate
items.clue: Solution added after acidifying; gives a white, cream or yellow solid with a halide.

questions.stem: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Its Mr is 60.0. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explanation: In 100 g: 3.33 mol C, about 6.6–6.7 mol H, 3.33 mol O. ÷ smallest: 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.stem: A student tests a solution for halide ions by adding silver nitrate solution acidified with dilute hydrochloric acid. A white precipitate forms. What can the student conclude?

options.text: The solution contains chloride ions, because AgCl is white.
The solution contains carbonate ions, because the acid did not remove them.
The solution contains no bromide or iodide, because the precipitate is not cream or yellow.
Nothing about chloride ions, because the hydrochloric acid itself added Cl⁻ ions.

questions.explanation: Right. The added Cl⁻ forms white AgCl whatever was in the sample. Repeat with dilute nitric acid.

questions.stem: Which statement about the relative ease of reduction of the halogens is correct?

options.text: Iodine is reduced more readily than bromine, as it is further down the group.
Bromine is reduced more readily than chlorine, as its nucleus has more protons.
Iodide ions are reduced more readily than iodine, as they are charged.
Chlorine is reduced more readily than bromine, as its atoms are smaller.

questions.explanation: An electron added to a chlorine atom is closer to the nucleus and less shielded, so it is held more strongly.

questions.stem: A compound of aluminium and sulfur contains 35.93% aluminium and 64.07% sulfur by mass. What is its empirical formula? Data: Ar Al 27.0, S 32.1.
questions.explanation: Divide each mass by its atomic mass: Al 1.33, S 2.00. Ratio 1 : 1.50; × 2 = 2 : 3.

questions.stem: An unknown sodium halide solution is acidified and silver nitrate is added. The precipitate does not dissolve in dilute ammonia solution, but does dissolve in concentrated ammonia solution. Which ion is present?
questions.explanation: AgBr (cream) dissolves only in concentrated ammonia. That matches both results.

questions.stem: Chlorine water is added to potassium iodide solution: Cl₂(aq) + 2I⁻(aq) → 2Cl⁻(aq) + I₂(aq). Which statement is correct?

options.text: Iodide ions are reduced, because they lose electrons.
Chlorine is the oxidising agent, and its oxidation number falls from 0 to −1.
Chlorine is oxidised, because it forms chloride ions.
Potassium ions are oxidised, because the solution turns brown.

questions.explanation: Cl₂ gains electrons from I⁻, so it is reduced and acts as the oxidising agent.

questions.stem: A hydrocarbon contains 88.80% carbon and 11.20% hydrogen by mass. Its Mr is 54.0. What is its molecular formula? (Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0)
Concentrated sulfuric acid is added separately to solid sodium bromide and to solid sodium iodide. Which product forms with sodium iodide but not with sodium bromide?
questions.explanation: Only iodide is a strong enough reducing agent to take sulfur from +6 all the way to −2 in H₂S (bad-egg smell).

questions.stem: A few drops of bromine water are added to a colourless solution containing both potassium chloride and potassium iodide, in excess. Cyclohexane is then added and the mixture shaken. What colour is the top layer, and why?

options.text: Pale green, because Br₂ oxidises Cl⁻ to Cl₂
Orange, because Br₂ reacts with neither halide and dissolves in the cyclohexane
Colourless, because Br₂ is reduced to colourless bromide ions
Violet, because Br₂ oxidises I⁻ to I₂ but cannot oxidise Cl⁻

questions.explanation: Br₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Br⁻ + I₂. Iodine dissolves in cyclohexane, giving violet. Cl⁻ is untouched.

questions.stem: Ethyne, a welding gas, and benzene, a liquid, both contain 92.3% carbon and 7.7% hydrogen by mass. What is the molecular formula of benzene? Data: Ar H 1.0, C 12.0. Mr of benzene = 78.0.
questions.explanation: C: 92.3 ÷ 12 ≈ 7.7; H: 7.7 ÷ 1 ≈ 7.7. Ratio 1 : 1, empirical formula CH (about 13). x = 78 ÷ 13 = 6: C₆H₆.

questions.stem: A solution contains both potassium chloride and potassium iodide. Acidified silver nitrate is added until no more precipitate forms. Then excess concentrated ammonia solution is added and the mixture is shaken. What is seen at the end?

options.text: A white precipitate and a yellow precipitate both remain
A cream precipitate remains and the solution is colourless
No precipitate remains and the solution is colourless

questions.explanation: Both AgCl and AgI form. Ammonia dissolves the AgCl but not the AgI, so the yellow precipitate is left.
